text: Drosophila Mind bomb (D-mib), an ortholog of zebrafish Mind bomb, is a RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes Notch signaling. Notch and its Delta/Serrate/LAG2 (DSL) ligands are central to this pathway regulating pattern formation during animal development. Delta is ubiquitinated by two unrelated E3 ligases—Neuralized (Drosophila, Xenopus) and Mind bomb (zebrafish)—both promoting Delta endocytosis and signaling. D-mib is required for multiple Neuralized-independent, Notch-dependent developmental processes and physically and functionally associates with both Serrate and Delta. Its ubiquitin ligase activity promotes DSL ligand activity, correlated with inducing endocytosis and degradation of Delta and Serrate (Le Borgne et al., 2005). D-mib functionally replaces Neuralized in cell fate decisions absolutely requiring endogenous Neuralized, showing highly similar activities of the unrelated ligases. Thus, ubiquitination of Delta and Serrate by Neuralized and D-mib is an obligate feature of DSL ligand activation throughout Drosophila development.
